conventions.convention: All matrix operations and phase norms act on numerical coefficients after fixing positive coordinate units s_i, time unit t_* and energy unit e_*. Physical positions, velocities and energies are reconstructed using those scales.

M is symmetric positive definite; K is symmetric without a sign restriction. Modal coordinates are z=OᵀM^(1/2)q, modal vectors are u_i=M^(-1/2)Oe_i, and Ku_i=λ_iMu_i. Positive, zero and negative λ_i respectively give oscillatory, affine and exponential scalar families.

Motion intervals have nonempty interior; derivatives at included endpoints are domain-relative. Free global-time claims concern the unique maximal extension on R, and coefficient values at zero are evaluated on that extension if the original interval omits zero.
The finite-time comparison uses displaced initial state ζ_0=(δq_0,v_0), δ=||ζ_0||>0 and δ exp(LT)<r_0. The linear phase solution is translated back by adding q_0 to its position component.

The forcing theorem assumes K≥0 and prescribed continuous J. A sinusoidal drive has Ω≥0; Ω=0 is the constant-force specialization, not an application of the earlier postulate's Ω>0 convention. Resonance requires a nonzero modal force component.

For weak damping ε is dimensionless, γ has mass/time units, ζ has length/time^(1/2) units, R, ρ and K have amplitude units, and A has time units. The averaging bound requires εK<ρ and the averaged trajectory to remain in the stated inner ball on [0,A/ε].

load_bearing.statement: Defines the coupled quadratic model Mq''+Kq=J with n≥1, symmetric positive definite M, symmetric K, prescribed continuous J, explicit numerical normalization, motions, phase system, quadratic energies, modal data and the small-oscillation model M(q_0), D²U(q_0) at a mechanical equilibrium.

For the free model with symmetric positive definite M and symmetric K, every datum has a unique global motion; motions are exactly the oscillatory, affine and hyperbolic modal families; energy splits into constant modal energies; pure-λ motions are intrinsically the solutions of q''+λq=0 in ker(K−λM); positive definite K bounds every motion, nonzero zero-mode slopes give unbounded motions, and a negative modal stiffness makes the rest point Lyapunov unstable.

For C³ positive definite kinetic metric and C³ potential at a mechanical equilibrium, the translated field is C² and has quadratic remainder and linear growth bounds on the stated ball. If δ>0 and δ exp(LT)<r_0, the nonlinear motion exists on [0,T] and satisfies ||z(t)−y(t)||≤Cδ²t exp((||A||+2L)t), with y the translated-back small-oscillation solution.

For symmetric positive definite M, symmetric non-negative K and continuous prescribed J, modal convolution formulas give the unique motion. For J=J_0 cos(Ωt), the stated particular solutions cover positive and zero modal stiffnesses; every motion is particular plus free. A nonzero resonant modal force makes every motion unbounded, whereas positive definite K and no driven resonant index make every motion bounded.

For mx''+εγx'+kx=0 with m,k,ε,γ>0, the rotating amplitude bijects global motions with ζ'=εF(t,ζ), whose average is −γζ/(2m). Under the explicit trapping and εK<ρ hypotheses, ||ζ−ζ̄||≤εK on [0,A/ε], and |E(t)−E_0 exp(−εγt/m)|≤mω_0εK(2|ζ_0|+εK).

For C² positive definite kinetic metric and C² potential at a strict local minimum, the Hessian is symmetric non-negative, the small-oscillation phase system is the derivative linearization, its motions have no exponential modal directions, and the nonlinear equilibrium is Lyapunov stable.

concerns.concern: Facts [F5] states that the translated equation z'=F(z) has initial value z(0)=z_0, although the item's z_0 is the original-chart datum (q_0+δq_0,v_0). It also writes the linear initial value as y(0)=z_0. The cited supplier requires the displaced datum (δq_0,v_0), whose norm is δ. The Statement and proof step 2.1 correctly use that displaced datum, so this is stale Facts wording rather than a defect in the proved conclusion.

The Example first uses M for the scalar middle mass and then writes 'M=diag(m,M,m)' for the mass metric. Subsequent expressions such as 2m/M and M-orthonormal reuse the same symbol in scalar and matrix roles. The computations are correct when the middle mass and mass matrix are distinguished, but the declared notation does not distinguish their types.

seams_checked.note: The scalar dictionary preserves m>0 and the harmonic, damping and prescribed-drive scopes. Zero stiffness is explicitly separated from the harmonic postulate's k>0, and constant forcing from its sinusoidal-drive postulate's Ω>0.
The kinetic metric DXᵀ𝕄DX and energy-per-coordinate generalized force agree with the opened coordinate dictionary; no stationarity-as-minimization inference is made.
Potential and mechanical-energy terminology preserves the declared potential representative and residual-force distinction. Free quadratic conservation is derived locally.

Prescribed external forcing retains its model-input status. Local-Lipschitz requirements are retained, and global linear existence comes from the linear supplier rather than general Newtonian local existence.
Coordinate dimensions and SI readings agree with the opened units and configuration definitions; explicit normalization prevents addition or matrix operations on unlike dimensional quantities.

Strict-minimum energy stability and derivative linearization retain their C² hypotheses. The non-negative-K modal supplier is not extended by citation to indefinite K; the latter construction is supplied explicitly.

Forced convolution, finite-time error and averaging statements retain their domains, sign restrictions, smallness and trapping conditions. The stale displaced-datum wording in Facts [F5] is recorded separately; the actual application is correct.

Lyapunov stability is used with maximal forward solutions and all-time existence. Nonlinear instability through the saddle supplier is restricted to hyperbolic derivatives with a positive-real-part eigenvalue.
The two-mass supplier's k≥0,c≥0 scope includes both the positive-coupling examples and the triatomic consistency check at zero coupling; its affine translation case is preserved.
Masses, stiffnesses, lengths, angles, drive coefficient and amplitude units are declared as model data. Numerical evaluations are explicitly distinguished from measurements.
Scalar oscillatory and repulsive classifications match their parameter cases. The averaging constants and cubic-error values independently evaluate to the reported decimals.
The inverted-pendulum nonlinear field is C¹ with eigenvalues ±sqrt(g/l), satisfying the opened hyperbolic-instability supplier. Other modal examples make only quadratic-model conclusions.
Stability, equilibrium and phase-norm vocabulary retain the numerical-coordinate and maximal-solution conventions.
Weak damping uses the declared linear-drag model conditionally. Prescribed sinusoidal and constant drives are distinguished, with no measured decay or apparatus-response claim.

The opened cm16 page preserves strict-minimum stability with degenerate Hessians, distinguishes linear from nonlinear instability, and describes linearization accuracy as a conditional finite-time estimate. It does not infer chaos, attraction or global approximation accuracy from cm09.
